lessons.title: 代词的定义与本质
lessons.meta: 用指向代替重复命名
examples: Amy is reading. She looks happy.
I saw a dog. It was wet.
This is my seat.
This book is mine.

analyses.label: 指示限定词+名词作主语

exampleNotes.title: 规则观察
exampleNotes.body: She 不重新命名人物，而是指回前面的 Amy，让表达不重复。

exampleNotes.title: 规则观察
exampleNotes.body: It 的意义来自前文 a dog；离开语境就不知道它指什么。

exampleNotes.title: 规则观察
exampleNotes.body: This 独立占据主语位置，所以这里是代词，不是修饰名词的限定词。

exampleNotes.title: 规则观察
exampleNotes.body: this 后面直接带 book，它限定“哪一本书”，这里不独立代替名词。

rules: 代词的核心是指向语境中的人、事物、范围或前文内容，避免反复命名。
代词的具体意义常依赖先行词或现场语境。
能独立占据名词短语位置的是代词；直接带名词的 this、my 等属于限定词用法。

questions.question: Amy is here. ___ is ready.
questions.correct: She 指回 Amy，并独立作主语。
questions.wrong: 再看规则：She 指回 Amy，并独立作主语。

questions.question: I found a key. ___ was under the desk.
questions.correct: It 指回单数事物 a key。
questions.wrong: 再看规则：It 指回单数事物 a key。

questions.question: 哪一项中的 this 是代词？
questions.correct: This 独立作主语时是代词。
questions.wrong: 再看规则：This 独立作主语时是代词。

questions.question: 哪一项中的 my 是限定词？
questions.correct: my 直接限定名词 bag。
questions.wrong: 再看规则：my 直接限定名词 bag。

narration.text:
如果一段话里不停地说 Amy、Amy、Amy，听起来会很累。英语会换一个短词，指回刚才那个人。看这两句。<#0.4#>Amy is reading。<#0.5#>She looks happy。<#0.8#>第二句里的 She 就像一根手指，指回前面的 Amy。它没有重新给人起名字，却让我们知道说的还是谁。这种用来指人、指物或指一段内容的词，叫代词。代词不是空词，它的具体意思要从前文或现场去找。<#0.8#>
再听。<#0.4#>I saw a dog。<#0.5#>It was wet。<#0.8#>It 指的是那只 dog。因为是一只动物，这里用 It；如果对象变成多个，代词也要跟着调整。可见，代词要和它指向的对象对得上。如果只冒出这一组的第二句，周围又有好几个可能对象，听者就会追问：它到底指谁？<#0.8#>
再比较两句。<#0.4#>This is my seat。<#0.5#>This book is mine。<#0.8#>第一句中 This 自己站在“谁或什么”的位置，代替一个对象，所以是代词。第二句的 this 后面紧跟 book，它只是帮我们锁定哪本书，不是独立代替 book。<#0.7#>
判断时先别背表格，连续问三件事：这个词指向谁或什么？听者能不能找到它指的对象？它有没有独立站在本来可以放名词短语的位置？三个问题都对上，再判断它在句中负责“谁”“什么”或其他工作。

lessons.title: 人称代词与格
lessons.meta: 谁参与，以及在句中做什么
examples: She helped me.
They spoke to him.
The teacher invited Tom and me.
You and I are partners.

exampleNotes.title: 规则观察
exampleNotes.body: She 是动作发出者，用主格；me 是 helped 的对象，用宾格。

exampleNotes.title: 规则观察
exampleNotes.body: him 跟在介词 to 后作介词宾语，因此不用 he。

exampleNotes.title: 规则观察
exampleNotes.body: Tom and me 整体作 invited 的宾语；去掉 Tom 后仍是 invited me。

exampleNotes.title: 规则观察
exampleNotes.body: You and I 整体作主语；去掉 you 后仍是 I am，而不是 me am。

rules: 人称代词先表示说话者、听话者或谈到的人和事，再根据句法功能选择格。
主格通常作主语；宾格作动词宾语或介词宾语。
并列结构不能靠礼貌口诀判断；去掉另一项，检查剩下的代词在句中做什么。

questions.question: ___ know the answer.
questions.correct: 空格作主语，应使用主格 They。
questions.wrong: 再看规则：空格作主语，应使用主格 They。

questions.question: Please wait for ___.
questions.correct: for 后作介词宾语，使用 us。
questions.wrong: 再看规则：for 后作介词宾语，使用 us。

questions.question: The coach praised Ben and ___.
questions.correct: Ben and me 整体作 praised 的宾语。
questions.wrong: 再看规则：Ben and me 整体作 praised 的宾语。

questions.question: ___ will present first.
questions.correct: 整个短语作主语，使用 I。
questions.wrong: 再看规则：整个短语作主语，使用 I。

narration.text: 两个人搬箱子，一个负责帮忙，一个接受帮助。英语要把这两个位置分清。<#0.4#>She helped me。<#0.8#>She 站在 helped 前，是发出动作的人；me 放在 helped 后，是动作落到的人。两者都指人，但句中任务不同，所以形式不同。作主语的 she 属于主格，作动词宾语的 me 属于宾格。<#0.7#>再听 They spoke to him。They 负责“谁说话”，用主格；him 跟在介词 to 后，作介词宾语，所以用宾格。判断格不能只盯着词离动词近不近，要看它到底占了主语位置，还是被动词、介词支配。<#0.8#>并列时最容易被“礼貌顺序”带偏。The teacher invited Tom and me 中，me 和 Tom 一起接受邀请，所以仍用宾格。You and I are partners 中，I 和 You 一起站在主语位置，所以用主格。<#0.7#>人称代词先区分说话者、听话者和谈到的第三方，再根据位置选格。操作时做两步：先问代词指的是谁；再暂时遮住并列的另一项，只看这个位置负责发出动作，还是接受动词或介词关系。

lessons.title: 物主限定词与物主代词
lessons.meta: 表达所属，但占据的位置不同
examples: My book is new.
This book is mine.
Her answer is different from ours.
A friend of mine called.

analyses.label: 物主限定词+名词作主语

exampleNotes.title: 规则观察
exampleNotes.body: my 只说明 book 属于谁，后面必须保留中心名词 book。

exampleNotes.title: 规则观察
exampleNotes.body: mine 独立表示 my book，已经包含“我的东西”这一层意思，后面不再接 book。

exampleNotes.title: 规则观察
exampleNotes.body: her 必须带 answer；ours 独立代替 our answer，避免重复。

exampleNotes.title: 规则观察
exampleNotes.body: a friend of mine 表示“我的朋友中的一位”，mine 不能换成 my。

rules: my/your/his/her/its/our/their 是物主限定词，必须和后面的名词共同构成名词短语。
mine/yours/his/hers/ours/theirs 是物主代词，可独立代替“物主限定词+名词”。
选择时看它是否需要独立占据名词短语位置，而不是只看中文都能译成“……的”。

questions.question: This is ___ desk.
questions.correct: desk 前需要物主限定词 our。
questions.wrong: 再看规则：desk 前需要物主限定词 our。

questions.question: Their room is large; ___ is small.
questions.correct: ours 独立代替 our room。
questions.wrong: 再看规则：ours 独立代替 our room。

questions.question: That coat is ___.
questions.correct: 空格后没有名词，使用物主代词 hers。
questions.wrong: 再看规则：空格后没有名词，使用物主代词 hers。

questions.question: He is a classmate of ___.
questions.correct: of 后用独立物主代词 mine。
questions.wrong: 再看规则：of 后用独立物主代词 mine。

narration.text: 几本书放在桌上，你拿起一本说 My book is new。my 像一张贴在 book 前的归属标签，必须带着后面的名词一起出现。语法上，my、your、her、our、their 这类叫物主限定词。<#0.8#>如果对方已经知道在谈 book，就可以说 This book is mine。mine 自己占满了“我的书”这个位置，后面不能再接 book。它叫物主代词，功能相当于 my book，但不是把两个词机械拼起来。<#0.7#>再看 Her answer is different from ours。Her 后有 answer，所以用限定形式；ours 跟在 from 后独立出现，指 our answer，所以用代词形式。A friend of mine called 里，mine 也独立放在 of 后，表示“我的朋友之一”，不能换成 my。<#0.8#>两组词中文都常译成“……的”，但英语看的是后面有没有中心名词。his 比较特殊，两种形式写法相同，仍要按位置判断任务；its 通常只作限定形式，英语没有与 mine 平行的独立物主代词。<#0.7#>选择时先看空格后：紧跟名词，就用限定形式；空格本身要代表“谁的某物”，就用独立形式。最后把被省略的名词补回心里读一遍，意思通顺再确定。

lessons.title: 反身代词
lessons.meta: 动作回到主语，或突出亲自完成
examples: She taught herself.
He looked at himself.
I made the cake myself.
The door opened by itself.

exampleNotes.title: 规则观察
exampleNotes.body: 教的人和被教的人都是 she，动作回到主语，所以用 herself。

exampleNotes.title: 规则观察
exampleNotes.body: at 后的对象仍是主语 he 本人，因此用 himself，不用 him。

exampleNotes.title: 规则观察
exampleNotes.body: the cake 才是 made 的宾语；myself 只强调“我亲自做”，不能把 it myself 合成一个宾语。

exampleNotes.title: 规则观察
exampleNotes.body: by itself 表示没有外力帮助，“门自己开了”。

rules: 主语与动词或介词后的对象指同一个人或事物时，使用反身代词。
反身代词也可作同位强调，删去后句子主干仍完整。
by oneself 表示独自或没有帮助，需结合语境判断。

questions.question: Leo cut ___.
questions.correct: Leo 是动作发出者也是承受者，用 himself。
questions.wrong: 再看规则：Leo 是动作发出者也是承受者，用 himself。

questions.question: She looked at ___ in the mirror.
questions.correct: 镜中的对象是主语本人，用 herself。
questions.wrong: 再看规则：镜中的对象是主语本人，用 herself。

questions.question: We painted the room ___.
questions.correct: ourselves 强调“我们亲自”，不是宾语。
questions.wrong: 再看规则：ourselves 强调“我们亲自”，不是宾语。

questions.question: The robot moved by ___.
questions.correct: by itself 表示机器人没有帮助而自行移动。
questions.wrong: 再看规则：by itself 表示机器人没有帮助而自行移动。

narration.text: 镜子前，一个女孩自己教自己弹琴。英语说 She taught herself。动作从 She 发出，又回到同一个人身上，所以不能用 her，而要用 herself。这个带 self 或 selves 的形式叫反身代词。<#0.8#>He looked at himself 也是同样的路线：He 是看的动作发出者，介词 at 后被看的人仍是他本人。即使中间隔着介词，只要动作对象和主语指向同一个人，就用反身形式。<#0.7#>但 I made the cake myself 里的 myself 不承担“做谁”的宾语，它只是强调蛋糕是我亲手做的。删掉 myself，I made the cake 仍然完整。这个用法叫同位强调，位置可以变化，主干不靠它补齐。<#0.8#>The door opened by itself 表示门没有外力帮助，自己开了。by oneself 有时强调独自一人，有时强调没有帮助，要根据场景判断。<#0.7#>操作时先画动作箭头：箭头从主语出发，又回到同一个对象，就用反身代词；若删掉它后主干仍完整，只是少了“亲自”的语气，就是强调用法；看到 by oneself，再问是在说独处，还是在说自行完成。

lessons.title: 指示代词
lessons.meta: 把注意力指向近处、远处或前文内容
examples: This is my key.
Those are ours.
This idea may work.
He missed the bus. That made him late.

exampleNotes.title: 规则观察
exampleNotes.body: This 指向说话者眼前的一个事物，并独立作主语。

exampleNotes.title: 规则观察
exampleNotes.body: Those 指向较远的多个事物，所以和复数 are 呼应。

exampleNotes.title: 规则观察
exampleNotes.body: This 后直接带 idea，这里限定“这个想法”，不是独立代词。

exampleNotes.title: 规则观察
exampleNotes.body: That 不指某个远处物体，而是概括前面“错过公交车”整件事。

rules: this/these 常指较近内容，that/those 常指较远内容；同时必须匹配单复数。
指示词独立占据名词短语位置时是代词；直接带名词时是限定词。
this/that 还可指向前文观点或事件，距离不一定是物理距离。

questions.question: ___ are my shoes over there.
questions.correct: 远处多个鞋子用 Those。
questions.wrong: 再看规则：远处多个鞋子用 Those。

questions.question: 哪一项中的 these 是代词？
questions.correct: These 独立作主语时是代词。
questions.wrong: 再看规则：These 独立作主语时是代词。

questions.question: I passed the test. ___ made me happy.
questions.correct: That 指代前面通过考试这件事。
questions.wrong: 再看规则：That 指代前面通过考试这件事。

questions.question: ___ book here is mine.
questions.correct: 近处单数名词 book 前用 This。
questions.wrong: 再看规则：近处单数名词 book 前用 This。

narration.text: 找钥匙时，你指着手边的一把说 This is my key；看向远处几双鞋，说 Those are ours。指示词像手指一样把注意力对准对象，同时还告诉听者距离和数量。this 指较近的一个，these 指较近的多个；that 指较远的一个，those 指较远的多个。<#0.8#>第一句中，This 后面没有名词，自己站在主语位置，代替眼前那件东西，所以是指示代词。<#0.7#>接着看 This idea may work。这里 This 紧贴 idea，只负责限定“这个想法”，整个 This idea 才是主语；它在这里是指示限定词。<#0.7#>距离也不一定拿尺子量。He missed the bus。That made him late。这里 That 不是指远处某个物品，而是把前面“错过公交车”整件事打包指回来。对话中 this 和 that 也能组织刚说过或将要说的信息。<#0.8#>判断时先找它指向什么，再核对一个还是多个、语境中较近还是较远；然后看后面是否直接带名词。独立占位置的是代词，带名词的是限定词。最后别忘了检查谓语，不能只顾远近忘了单复数。

lessons.title: 疑问代词
lessons.meta: 用未知项占据句中位置
examples: Who called you?
Whom did you speak to?
Whose bag is this?
Which do you prefer, tea or coffee?

analyses.label: 疑问限定词+名词作表语

exampleNotes.title: 规则观察
exampleNotes.body: Who 占据“谁打电话”中的主语位置，所以后面直接接 called。

exampleNotes.title: 规则观察
exampleNotes.body: Whom 是 to 的对象，只因疑问结构移到句首；did 承担疑问，you 仍是主语。日常英语常用 who。

exampleNotes.title: 规则观察
exampleNotes.body: this 是被询问的事物，作主语；Whose bag 询问它是谁的包，作表语。

exampleNotes.title: 规则观察
exampleNotes.body: Which 是 prefer 的宾语，因疑问移到句首；tea or coffee 给出限定选择范围。what 通常用于开放范围。

rules: 疑问代词不是问句外的标签，而是在问句内部承担主语、宾语或表语等成分。
who 通常问人；whom 是宾格形式，正式语体中更常见；whose 询问所属。
which 面向限定范围选择，what 通常面向开放范围询问事物或内容。

questions.question: ___ broke the window?
questions.correct: 空格作 broke 的主语，用 Who。
questions.wrong: 再看规则：空格作 broke 的主语，用 Who。

questions.question: To ___ did you send it?
questions.correct: 正式表达中介词 To 后使用宾格 whom。
questions.wrong: 再看规则：正式表达中介词 To 后使用宾格 whom。

questions.question: ___ coat is yours?
questions.correct: 询问所属用 Whose。
questions.wrong: 再看规则：询问所属用 Whose。

questions.question: ___ do you want, the red one or the blue one?
questions.correct: 选项范围已给出，用 Which。
questions.wrong: 再看规则：选项范围已给出，用 Which。

narration.text: 电话响了却不知道来电人，你问 Who called you？Who 不是站在句子外贴个“问人”标签，它正占着“谁打来电话”的主语位置，所以后面直接接 called，不需要再添一个主语。这样的疑问词在句内代替未知项，叫疑问代词。<#0.8#>Whom did you speak to？想问的是你和谁说话。you 才是主语，whom 是介词 to 的对象，只因问句结构移到前面。正式语体，尤其介词前置时常用 whom；日常口语中常听到 who。<#0.7#>Whose bag is this 询问所属。这里 this 是要辨认的物品，Whose bag 说明它是谁的包。whose 后带 bag 时有类似限定的作用，但核心仍是把未知的所有者问出来。<#0.8#>桌上只有茶和咖啡两项，问 Which do you prefer, tea or coffee？Which 面向已经限定的范围；如果选项开放，问“你想要什么”，通常用 what。<#0.7#>操作时先把问句还原成带空格的陈述关系：谁做动作，用 who；动作或介词指向谁，正式表达可用 whom；问所属用 whose；给定范围里选用 which，开放询问用 what。再确认疑问词在句内究竟作主语、宾语还是表语。

lessons.title: 不定代词：未知人和事物
lessons.meta: some · any · no · every 系列
examples: Someone is waiting.
I did not see anything.
Would you like something to drink?
Nobody knows the answer.

exampleNotes.title: 规则观察
exampleNotes.body: Someone 表示某个身份未说明的人，语法上按单数处理。

exampleNotes.title: 规则观察
exampleNotes.body: 否定已经由 not 表达，anything 保持“任何东西”的开放范围。

exampleNotes.title: 规则观察
exampleNotes.body: 虽然是问句，说话者是在积极提供饮料，因此自然用 something。

exampleNotes.title: 规则观察
exampleNotes.body: Nobody 本身已经表示“没有人”，不能再加 not；谓语用单数 knows。

rules: some 系列常表示存在某个对象；any 系列把范围打开到任何对象，常见于疑问、否定和条件语境。
some 也可用于期待肯定回应的请求或提议，不能机械套“问句只用 any”。
no-/every-/-one/-body/-thing 复合不定代词通常按单数一致；no 系列自身已含否定。

questions.question: ___ left a message for you.
questions.correct: 肯定句表示某个未知的人，用 Someone。
questions.wrong: 再看规则：肯定句表示某个未知的人，用 Someone。

questions.question: I don't need ___.
questions.correct: not 已表达否定，使用 anything，避免双重否定。
questions.wrong: 再看规则：not 已表达否定，使用 anything，避免双重否定。

questions.question: Would you like ___ to eat?
questions.correct: 提议并期待肯定回应，常用 something。
questions.wrong: 再看规则：提议并期待肯定回应，常用 something。

questions.question: Everyone ___ ready.
questions.correct: Everyone 语法上按单数处理。
questions.wrong: 再看规则：Everyone 语法上按单数处理。

narration.text: 门外传来脚步声，你知道有人，却不知道是谁，可以说 Someone is waiting。Someone 不给出具体身份，只确认“存在某个人”；这类把人或事物留在不确定范围里的词，叫不定代词。它在句中作主语，通常按单数处理，所以用 is。<#0.8#>I did not see anything 里，not 已经表达否定，anything 把范围打开成“任何东西”，合起来就是“什么也没看见”。这里否定已经表达完整，不能再叠加另一个否定词。<#0.7#>问句并非永远只能用 any。端着饮料招待客人时说 Would you like something to drink？说话者在积极提供某样东西，也期待对方接受，所以 something 很自然。普通询问信息、否定或条件中，any 系列更常见。<#0.7#>最后看 Nobody knows the answer。Nobody 自己已经含“没有人”，后面不再加 not，而且它在句中作主语，基础用法配单数 knows。<#0.8#>判断时先看说话者是在确认某个对象存在，还是把范围开放到任何对象；再看否定是否已经由 not 或 no 系列承担；最后检查谓语一致。

lessons.title: 不定代词：数量与范围
lessons.meta: all · both · each · either · neither · none
examples: Both are correct.
Either will work.
Neither of the answers is correct.
Each has a ticket.
All of the students are ready.
All of the water is clean.
None of the water is left.
None of the students are absent.

analyses.label: 全部不可数范围作主语
零数量不可数范围作主语
零数量复数范围作主语

exampleNotes.title: 规则观察
exampleNotes.body: Both 把两个对象一起纳入，因而使用复数 are。

exampleNotes.title: 规则观察
exampleNotes.body: Either 从两个对象中任选一个，所以基础用法按单数处理。

exampleNotes.title: 规则观察
exampleNotes.body: Neither 表示两个选项中没有一个；规范基础用法通常接单数谓语。

exampleNotes.title: 规则观察
exampleNotes.body: Each 把成员一个一个看，所以即使涉及多人，谓语仍用单数 has。

exampleNotes.title: 规则观察
exampleNotes.body: All 指向复数 students 的全体，因此使用复数 are。

exampleNotes.title: 规则观察
exampleNotes.body: All 指向不可数 water 的全部数量，因此使用单数 is。

exampleNotes.title: 规则观察
exampleNotes.body: None 指 water 这一不可数范围中一点也没有，因此使用 is。

exampleNotes.title: 规则观察
exampleNotes.body: None 指 students 中零个人缺席；这里按复数集合自然使用 are。

rules: both 把两个对象都纳入，作主语时使用复数一致。
either 表示两者中的任意一个，基础用法通常按单数一致。
neither 表示两者中一个也没有，基础用法通常按单数一致。
each 把成员逐个看待，通常使用单数一致。
all 表示整个范围，谓语由它所指的复数集合或不可数数量决定。
none 表示数量为零，谓语结合 of 后名词与语境判断，不是“永远单数”。

questions.question: The two answers are good. ___ are acceptable.
questions.correct: 两个都可接受，用 Both，并配复数 are。
questions.wrong: 再看规则：两个都可接受，用 Both，并配复数 are。

questions.question: There are two doors. ___ is suitable.
questions.correct: 表示两扇门中任意一扇都合适，用 Either 和单数 is。
questions.wrong: 再看规则：表示两扇门中任意一扇都合适，用 Either 和单数 is。

questions.question: ___ of the two answers is correct.
questions.correct: 两个答案都不正确，用 Neither。
questions.wrong: 再看规则：两个答案都不正确，用 Neither。

questions.question: ___ of the students has a card.
questions.correct: 逐个学生看并使用 has，用 Each。
questions.wrong: 再看规则：逐个学生看并使用 has，用 Each。

questions.question: All of the students ___ ready.
questions.correct: All 指复数 students 的全体，用 are。
questions.wrong: 再看规则：All 指复数 students 的全体，用 are。

questions.question: All of the milk ___ fresh.
questions.correct: All 指不可数 milk 的全部，用 is。
questions.wrong: 再看规则：All 指不可数 milk 的全部，用 is。

questions.question: None of the water ___ left.
questions.correct: water 不可数，使用 is。
questions.wrong: 再看规则：water 不可数，使用 is。

questions.question: None of the players ___ injured.
questions.correct: 这里指复数 players 中零人受伤，使用 are。
questions.wrong: 再看规则：这里指复数 players 中零人受伤，使用 are。

narration.text: 桌上有两个答案。说 Both are correct，是把两个一起纳入，所以 Both 配复数 are；说 Either will work，是从两个里任选一个，视角落在“一个”上，基础用法配单数。Neither of the answers is correct 则表示两个中一个也不对，通常也按单数处理。<#0.8#>换成一排学生，Each has a ticket。虽然现场有很多人，Each 像镜头逐个扫过，每次只看一个成员，所以用单数 has。这里决定谓语的不是现实总人数，而是词怎样切分这个范围。<#0.7#>All 要看它后面装的是什么。All of the students are ready 指整个复数学生集合，用 are；All of the water is clean 指全部水量，water 不可数，用 is。<#0.8#>None 表示数量为零，却不是“永远单数”。None of the water is left 跟不可数 water 用 is；None of the students are absent 把复数集合中的缺席人数说成零，用 are 很自然。<#0.7#>判断时先画范围：刚好两个，区分 both、either、neither；逐个看用 each；整个范围用 all；零数量用 none。然后看 of 后的中心名词是复数集合还是不可数数量，再决定谓语。不要只背中文“都、任一、都不”，要看镜头是合看、选一个、逐个看还是看零个。

lessons.title: it 的指代与形式作用
lessons.meta: 有时指具体事物，有时只撑起结构
examples: I bought a phone. It works well.
It is raining.
It is five o’clock.
It is three kilometres to the station.
It is important to rest.
I find it easy to learn online.

exampleNotes.title: 规则观察
exampleNotes.body: It 明确指回 a phone，可以回答“什么运行得好”。

exampleNotes.title: 规则观察
exampleNotes.body: 这里没有一个具体事物叫 it；英语句子需要主语位置，it 只承担结构作用。

exampleNotes.title: 规则观察
exampleNotes.body: It 不指某个东西，只让英语能用完整句子说明当前时间。

exampleNotes.title: 规则观察
exampleNotes.body: It 不代替 station，而是支撑“到车站有三公里”这个距离结构。

exampleNotes.title: 规则观察
exampleNotes.body: 真正要评价的是 to rest；it 先占主语位置，把较长内容放到句尾。

exampleNotes.title: 规则观察
exampleNotes.body: find 真正涉及的是 to learn online；it 先作形式宾语，让 easy 紧跟其后。

rules: 指代 it 必须能在语境中找到具体先行词。
天气、时间、距离等表达中的 it 通常不指具体对象，只满足英语主语结构。
形式主语或形式宾语 it 把较长的不定式或从句后移；真正内容仍在后面。

questions.question: I found a wallet. ___ was empty.
questions.correct: It 指回前面的单数 wallet。
questions.wrong: 再看规则：It 指回前面的单数 wallet。

questions.question: ___ is snowing.
questions.correct: 天气表达用无具体指向的 It。
questions.wrong: 再看规则：天气表达用无具体指向的 It。

questions.question: ___ is six o’clock.
questions.correct: 说明时间时用形式主语 It。
questions.wrong: 再看规则：说明时间时用形式主语 It。

questions.question: ___ is two miles to the beach.
questions.correct: 说明距离时用形式主语 It。
questions.wrong: 再看规则：说明距离时用形式主语 It。

questions.question: ___ is useful to review daily.
questions.correct: It 作形式主语，真正主语是 to review daily。
questions.wrong: 再看规则：It 作形式主语，真正主语是 to review daily。

questions.question: We think ___ necessary to leave now.
questions.correct: it 作形式宾语，真正内容是 to leave now。
questions.wrong: 再看规则：it 作形式宾语，真正内容是 to leave now。

narration.text: 刚买了一部手机，接着说 I bought a phone。It works well。这里 It 明确指回前面的 a phone，听者能回答“什么运行得好”。这种 it 有具体先行词，承担真正的指代任务。<#0.8#>但窗外下雨时说 It is raining，并没有某个东西叫 it。英语完整句子通常需要主语位置，天气表达就让 it 先把这个位置撑起来。It is five o'clock 表时间，It is three kilometres to the station 表距离，也都不指某件具体物品。<#0.8#>还有一种情况是把太长的内容往后放。It is important to rest 中，真正被评价为 important 的是 to rest；it 先作形式主语，让句子头部轻一些。I find it easy to learn online 里，find 真正涉及的内容是 to learn online，it 先占形式宾语位置，easy 才能自然紧跟。<#0.7#>术语上，要分指代 it、天气时间距离中的无指向 it，以及形式主语或形式宾语 it。<#0.7#>判断时先追问“it 到底指谁或什么”。能在前文找到唯一对象，就是指代用法；找不到，再看是否在说天气、时间、距离；若后面还有不定式或从句，试着把它移到前面，能还原真正内容，就按形式成分分析。

lessons.title: 关系代词的双重任务
lessons.meta: 连接从句，同时在从句内代替先行词
examples: The girl who sings is Amy.
The book that I bought is useful.
The boy whose bike was lost is sad.
The place where we met is nearby.

analyses.label: 关系代词作从句主语的定语从句
关系代词作从句宾语的定语从句
关系副词引导的定语从句

exampleNotes.title: 语序翻译
exampleNotes.body: who 既指回 girl，又在 sings 前作主语；中文把“唱歌的”移到“女孩”前。

exampleNotes.title: 语序翻译
exampleNotes.body: that 指回 book，并在 I bought ___ 中补上宾语位置；中文译为“我买的书”。

exampleNotes.title: 语序翻译
exampleNotes.body: whose 表示 bike 属于 boy，整个从句后置修饰 boy。

exampleNotes.title: 语序翻译
exampleNotes.body: where 在从句中表示地点，不是关系代词；它和 who/which 的句内任务不同。

rules: 关系代词一头连接先行词与定语从句，一头在从句内部作主语、宾语或定语。
who 通常指人，which 指物，that 可指人或物，whose 表所属；选择还要看从句内缺什么成分。
where/when/why 是关系副词，表达地点、时间或原因，不应与关系代词混作一类。

questions.question: The woman ___ teaches us is kind.
questions.correct: 先行词是人，且从句缺主语，用 who。
questions.wrong: 再看规则：先行词是人，且从句缺主语，用 who。

questions.question: The film ___ we watched was funny.
questions.correct: that 指回 film，并作 watched 的宾语。
questions.wrong: 再看规则：that 指回 film，并作 watched 的宾语。

questions.question: The student ___ project won smiled.
questions.correct: project 与 student 是所属关系，用 whose。
questions.wrong: 再看规则：project 与 student 是所属关系，用 whose。

questions.question: 哪一项是关系副词？
questions.correct: where 在从句中表达地点，是关系副词。
questions.wrong: 再看规则：where 在从句中表达地点，是关系副词。

narration.text: 人群里要说明“那个唱歌的女孩”，英语说 The girl who sings is Amy。who 一头指回 girl，把后面的说明接到女孩身上；另一头又站在 sings 前，承担“谁唱歌”的主语。一个词同时连接外面的名词和填补从句内部位置，这就是关系代词的双重任务。<#0.8#>The book that I bought is useful 里，that 指回 book；从句 I bought 后缺少“买了什么”，that 在内部作宾语。选择关系词不能只看先行词是人还是物，还要检查从句究竟缺主语、宾语还是所属成分。<#0.8#>The boy whose bike was lost is sad 中，whose 把 bike 与 boy 的所属关系带进从句，意思是“他的自行车丢了”。who 常指人，which 常指物，that 可以指人或物，whose 表所属，但具体选择还受句子结构限制。<#0.7#>The place where we met is nearby 的 where 表示“在那里”，在从句中承担地点关系，它是关系副词，不是关系代词；when 和 why 也分别表达时间、原因。<#0.7#>判断时先圈出先行词，再遮住关系词读从句：缺人或物的主语、宾语、所属，就选合适的关系代词；主干成分完整，只缺地点、时间或原因关系，再考虑 where、when、why。

lessons.title: 相互代词
lessons.meta: 多个参与者彼此施加动作
examples: The twins help each other.
The players talked to one another.
They looked at themselves.

exampleNotes.title: 规则观察
exampleNotes.body: 每个双胞胎都帮助另一个，动作在不同参与者之间双向发生。

exampleNotes.title: 规则观察
exampleNotes.body: one another 是 to 的宾语，表示队员彼此交谈。

exampleNotes.title: 规则观察
exampleNotes.body: themselves 表示每个人看自己，不是彼此看；这与 each other 不同。

rules: each other 和 one another 都表示不同参与者之间的相互作用，现代英语中通常可以互换。
相互代词与反身代词的关键差别是：动作流向别人，还是返回各自主语自身。

questions.question: The two friends trust ___.
questions.correct: 两人彼此信任，用 each other。
questions.wrong: 再看规则：两人彼此信任，用 each other。

questions.question: The children introduced themselves.
questions.correct: themselves 表示每个孩子介绍自己。
questions.wrong: 再看规则：themselves 表示每个孩子介绍自己。

questions.question: The teams competed with ___.
questions.correct: 多个队伍彼此竞争，用 one another。
questions.wrong: 再看规则：多个队伍彼此竞争，用 one another。

narration.text: 双胞胎一起做作业，一个帮另一个，另一个也帮回来，可以说 The twins help each other。动作不是各自回到自己身上，而是在两个参与者之间来回流动。each other 这种表示彼此作用的形式，叫相互代词。<#0.8#>The players talked to one another 也把说话动作连到其他队员。现代英语中 each other 和 one another 通常可以互换，不必机械规定“两个人只能用前者、三个人以上只能用后者”；真正重要的是场景里至少有不同参与者互相发生作用。<#0.8#>对比 They looked at themselves。这里每个人看的对象是自己，动作分别返回各自主语，所以用反身代词 themselves。前两句是参与者彼此作用，第三句是动作回到各自本人。<#0.7#>判断时画箭头最直接：箭头从一个参与者指向另一个，同时反向发生，用相互代词；箭头从每个主语绕回自己，用反身代词。若动词本身需要介词，还要把介词连同关系一起保留。

lessons.title: one、ones 与 other 系列
lessons.meta: 代替同类名词，不等于指回同一个事物
examples: My pen is broken; I need a new one.
These shoes are tight; show me the larger ones.
This cup is dirty; give me another.
One answer is correct; the other is wrong.

analyses.label: one 替代 pen 作宾语
ones 替代 shoes 作直接宾语

exampleNotes.title: 规则观察
exampleNotes.body: one 代替同类名词 pen，意思是另一支笔，不是原来那支。

exampleNotes.title: 规则观察
exampleNotes.body: ones 代替复数 shoes，larger 保留对这类鞋的限定。

exampleNotes.title: 规则观察
exampleNotes.body: another 表示同类中的“再一个/另一个”单数对象，相当于 another cup。

exampleNotes.title: 规则观察
exampleNotes.body: 范围只有两个，one 提出一个，the other 指剩下的那个。

rules: one/ones 替代前面提到的可数名词类别，通常指同类但不是同一个对象；it 通常回指同一个具体对象。
another 表示不确定范围中的另一个或再一个单数对象。
两者中用 one...the other；多者中可用 one...another...the others 表达不同范围。

questions.question: My phone is old. I need a new ___.
questions.correct: 需要同类的新手机，用 one，不是原来的 it。
questions.wrong: 再看规则：需要同类的新手机，用 one，不是原来的 it。

questions.question: I like the blue shoes, not the red ___.
questions.correct: 替代复数 shoes 用 ones。
questions.wrong: 再看规则：替代复数 shoes 用 ones。

questions.question: This chair is wet. Bring me ___.
questions.correct: 另拿一把单数椅子，用 another。
questions.wrong: 再看规则：另拿一把单数椅子，用 another。

questions.question: There are two keys. One is mine; ___ is yours.
questions.correct: 两个中的剩下一个用 the other。
questions.wrong: 再看规则：两个中的剩下一个用 the other。

narration.text: 手里的笔坏了，你想买一支新的，页面说 My pen is broken；I need a new one。one 代替的是 pen 这一类名词，指同类中的另一支，不是原来那支。<#0.8#>These shoes are tight；show me the larger ones。前面是复数 shoes，所以用 ones，larger 继续说明要同类鞋中更大的那些。one 和 ones 都替代可数名词类别，但要跟着单复数变化。<#0.7#>杯子脏了，要求再拿一个，页面是 This cup is dirty；give me another。another 表示开放范围里的“再一个”或“另一个”单数对象，后面不必重复 cup。<#0.8#>如果范围明确只有两个，就用 One answer is correct；the other is wrong。one 先提出一个，the other 锁定剩下的那个。多于两个时，范围和数量还要随语境继续判断。<#0.7#>操作时先问代词是在指回原来的具体对象，还是替代同类中的另一个；再看单数还是复数、范围是否恰好两个。同类单数或复数看 one、ones，开放范围的另一个看 another，两个中的剩余项看 the other。

lessons.title: 代词与先行词一致
lessons.meta: 人称、数量与所知信息相配
examples: Lucy said she was ready.
The students finished their work.
If anyone calls, tell them I am busy.
Every student should bring their ID.

analyses.label: 宾语从句中的回指代词
谓语与单数 they 宾语
单数 they 的物主形式

exampleNotes.title: 规则观察
exampleNotes.body: she 与 Lucy 在人称、单数和已知性别信息上匹配。

exampleNotes.title: 规则观察
exampleNotes.body: their 指回复数 students，因此不能换成 his 或 her。

exampleNotes.title: 规则观察
exampleNotes.body: anyone 的具体性别未知，现代标准英语常用单数 they/them 自然回指。

exampleNotes.title: 规则观察
exampleNotes.body: Every student 逐个看是单数，但性别不限；their 可作包容、自然的单数回指。

rules: 代词应与先行词在人称和数量上相配，并尊重语境中已经明确的信息。
先行词为复数时使用复数代词；不要因中间出现单数名词而误判。
性别未知、不重要或对象使用 they 时，单数 they/them/their 是现代标准英语的自然选择；同一语境保持一致。

questions.question: Mia said ___ would help.
questions.correct: Mia 是已知单数女性；空格作从句主语，用 she。
questions.wrong: 再看规则：Mia 是已知单数女性；空格作从句主语，用 she。

questions.question: The boys packed ___ bags.
questions.correct: 先行词 boys 是复数，用 their。
questions.wrong: 再看规则：先行词 boys 是复数，用 their。

questions.question: Someone left ___ umbrella.
questions.correct: umbrella 前需要限定形式；性别未知时用单数 their。
questions.wrong: 再看规则：umbrella 前需要限定形式；性别未知时用单数 their。

questions.question: Every visitor must show ___ ticket.
questions.correct: their 包容地回指 every visitor。
questions.wrong: 再看规则：their 包容地回指 every visitor。

narration.text: 接力传话时，代词必须把信息准确交回前面的对象。Lucy said she was ready。she 指回 Lucy，两者都是第三人称单数，语境也已经说明是 Lucy，所以读者不会换错人。这个被代词指回的对象叫先行词，代词要和它在人称、数量及已知信息上协调。<#0.8#>The students finished their work 中，先行词 students 是复数，物主形式就用 their。即使中间出现 work 这样的单数名词，也不能改用 its，因为决定代词的是它真正指向谁，不是离它最近的词。<#0.8#>如果说 If anyone calls, tell them I am busy，anyone 形式上按单数处理，但来电者的性别未知，现代标准英语自然使用单数 they 的宾格 them。Every student should bring their ID 也是逐个学生，却不限定性别，their 是包容而标准的回指。<#0.7#>单数 they 不等于把先行词变成复数；谓语和其他表达仍要按各自结构判断，并在同一语境保持代词形式一致。<#0.7#>检查时先用箭头连出每个代词的先行词，再核对第一、第二、第三人称和单复数；性别未知、不重要或对象使用 they 时，可选 they、them、their。最后从头读一遍，确认没有被中间名词带偏。

lessons.title: 指代清晰与歧义
lessons.meta: 读者应能立刻知道代词指谁
examples: When Tom met Jack, he smiled.
When Tom met Jack, Tom smiled.
Put the vase on the table and clean it.
Students lose focus when they are tired.

analyses.label: 时间从句含两个男性名词
清晰回指 students 的时间从句

exampleNotes.title: 规则观察
exampleNotes.body: Tom 和 Jack 都可能是 he，语法形式正确，但读者无法确定谁笑了。

exampleNotes.title: 规则观察
exampleNotes.body: 重复 Tom 虽不如代词短，却准确说明笑的人，清晰优先于避免重复。

exampleNotes.title: 规则观察
exampleNotes.body: it 可能指 vase，也可能指 table；应改成 clean the vase 或 clean the table。

exampleNotes.title: 规则观察
exampleNotes.body: they 前面只有合适的复数人物 students，指向清楚，无须重复名词。

rules: 代词附近若有多个在人称和数量上都匹配的先行词，形式一致仍可能产生意义歧义。
消除歧义最直接的方法是重复关键名词或改写句子，不要为了少重复牺牲清晰。
清晰不是禁止代词；当前文只有一个合理先行词时，代词能自然衔接信息。

questions.question: “Lily told Anna that she won.” 的问题是什么？
questions.correct: Lily 和 Anna 都可能是 she。
questions.wrong: 再看规则：Lily 和 Anna 都可能是 she。

questions.question: Which is clearer?

options.text: When Ben called Leo, Ben apologized.
When Ben called Leo, he apologized.

questions.correct: 重复 Ben 明确说明道歉者。
questions.wrong: 再看规则：重复 Ben 明确说明道歉者。

questions.question: Move the box beside the chair and paint it. What should you do?
questions.correct: box 和 chair 都可能是 it，应重复目标名词。
questions.wrong: 再看规则：box 和 chair 都可能是 it，应重复目标名词。

questions.question: The players rested because they were tired. Is they clear?
questions.correct: players 是唯一合理的复数人物先行词。
questions.wrong: 再看规则：players 是唯一合理的复数人物先行词。

narration.text: Tom 遇见 Jack 之后，有人笑了。若只写 When Tom met Jack, he smiled，he 在人称和单数上同时匹配 Tom 与 Jack，语法形式没有错，画面却有两个可能答案。读者不知道是谁笑，这就是指代歧义。<#0.8#>最直接的修复就是页面第二句 When Tom met Jack, Tom smiled。虽然重复了 Tom，却换来了唯一明确的意思。代词的价值是减少重复，但清楚永远比少写一个词更重要。<#0.7#>再看 Put the vase on the table and clean it。it 既可能指 vase，也可能指 table。要消除歧义，就应重复真正要清洁的对象，不能指望读者猜场景。<#0.8#>不过清晰不等于禁止代词。Students lose focus when they are tired 中，前面只有 students 是合理的复数人物先行词，they 指向唯一，使用自然。<#0.7#>检查时从每个代词向前找所有在人称、数量和意义上可能匹配的对象。若候选超过一个，就重复目标名词、调整语序或拆句；若只有一个合理候选，保留代词即可。最后让句子脱离你脑中的画面再读一次，看陌生读者能否立刻确定指向。

lessons.title: 代词综合判断
lessons.meta: 先找指向，再看句中位置和范围
examples: Every runner checked their number themselves.
I lost my umbrella, so I bought another.
The teacher asked who had finished. Two students raised their hands.
This is the book that I need.
Nina spoke to Emma after Nina arrived.

analyses.label: 疑问词引导的宾语从句
关系代词引导后置定语

exampleNotes.title: 规则观察
exampleNotes.body: their 包容地回指 every runner；themselves 强调每位跑者亲自核对，两个代词任务不同。

exampleNotes.title: 规则观察
exampleNotes.body: my 必须带 umbrella；another 独立表示“另一把伞”，避免再次重复 umbrella。

exampleNotes.title: 规则观察
exampleNotes.body: who 在从句中询问未知的人；their 再清楚回指 two students。

exampleNotes.title: 语序翻译
exampleNotes.body: This 指眼前事物；that 指回 book 并作 need 的宾语。中文把“我需要的”移到“书”前。

exampleNotes.title: 规则观察
exampleNotes.body: 如果写 she，可能指 Nina 或 Emma；重复 Nina 让读者立即确定到达的人。

rules: 判断代词先问三件事：它指向什么、在句中做什么、表达的是同一对象还是同类替代。
同一句可以出现多种代词；必须逐个判断，不能只按中文译词选择。
最终检查指代是否一致且唯一可识别；不清楚时重复名词比勉强使用代词更好。

questions.question: Every child packed ___ own lunch.
questions.correct: their 包容地回指 every child。
questions.wrong: 再看规则：their 包容地回指 every child。

questions.question: This cup is cracked. Please bring me ___.
questions.correct: 需要另一只同类杯子，用 another。
questions.wrong: 再看规则：需要另一只同类杯子，用 another。

questions.question: The woman ___ called is my aunt.
questions.correct: who 指回 woman，并在从句中作主语。
questions.wrong: 再看规则：who 指回 woman，并在从句中作主语。

questions.question: Nina spoke to Emma after ___ arrived. Which is clearest?
questions.correct: 重复 Nina 消除 she 可能指两人的歧义。
questions.wrong: 再看规则：重复 Nina 消除 she 可能指两人的歧义。

narration.text: 赛前，每位跑者亲自核对号码，可以说 Every runner checked their number themselves。their 指回 every runner，放在 number 前表示所属；themselves 不是宾语，而是强调跑者亲自核对。两个代词靠得很近，任务却完全不同，不能只按中文“他们的、他们自己”机械选词。<#0.8#>I lost my umbrella, so I bought another 里，my 必须带 umbrella；another 独立表示同类中的另一把伞，不是找回原来那把。先问同一个对象还是同类替代，才能在 it 和 another 之间选对。<#0.8#>The teacher asked who had finished。who 在从句内部占主语位置，询问未知的人；下一句 Two students raised their hands，their 又清楚指回复数 students。每出现一个代词，都要重新建立自己的指向和句中任务。<#0.7#>This is the book that I need 中，This 指现场事物，that 一头连 book，一头作 need 的宾语。Nina spoke to Emma after Nina arrived 则故意重复 Nina，因为换成 she 会让两个女性名字都成为候选。<#0.7#>综合判断按三步：先给每个代词画出指向；再看它在句中作主语、宾语、限定、强调还是连接；最后判断它表示原对象、同类替代还是相互关系。完成后再做一次清晰度检查，候选不唯一就重复名词。

en.title: Pronouns · 15 lessons
en.copy: Master the core rules, then handle complex contexts.

course.title: Definition and core of pronouns
course.meta: Reference instead of repeated naming
examples: Amy is reading. She looks happy.
I saw a dog. It was wet.
This is my seat.
This book is mine.

exampleNotes.title: Rule focus
exampleNotes.body: She points back to Amy instead of naming her again.

exampleNotes.title: Rule focus
exampleNotes.body: It gets its meaning from a dog; without context its referent is unknown.

exampleNotes.title: Rule focus
exampleNotes.body: This occupies the subject slot by itself, so it is a pronoun here.

exampleNotes.title: Rule focus
exampleNotes.body: this directly determines book, so it does not replace the noun here.

rules: A pronoun points to a person, thing, range or earlier idea and avoids repeated naming.
A pronoun often depends on an antecedent or the situation for its meaning.
A form used independently in a noun-phrase slot is a pronoun; this or my directly before a noun functions as a determiner.

questions.question: Amy is here. ___ is ready.
questions.correct: She refers back to Amy and functions as subject.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: She refers back to Amy and functions as subject.

questions.question: I found a key. ___ was under the desk.
questions.correct: It refers back to the singular thing a key.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: It refers back to the singular thing a key.

questions.question: In which option is this a pronoun?
questions.correct: This is a pronoun when it stands alone as subject.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: This is a pronoun when it stands alone as subject.

questions.question: In which option is my a determiner?
questions.correct: my directly determines bag.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: my directly determines bag.

narration.text:
如果一段话里不停地说 Amy、Amy、Amy，听起来会很累。英语会换一个短词，指回刚才那个人。看这两句。<#0.4#>Amy is reading。<#0.5#>She looks happy。<#0.8#>第二句里的 She 就像一根手指，指回前面的 Amy。它没有重新给人起名字，却让我们知道说的还是谁。这种用来指人、指物或指一段内容的词，叫代词。代词不是空词，它的具体意思要从前文或现场去找。<#0.8#>
再听。<#0.4#>I saw a dog。<#0.5#>It was wet。<#0.8#>It 指的是那只 dog。因为是一只动物，这里用 It；如果对象变成多个，代词也要跟着调整。可见，代词要和它指向的对象对得上。如果只冒出这一组的第二句，周围又有好几个可能对象，听者就会追问：它到底指谁？<#0.8#>
再比较两句。<#0.4#>This is my seat。<#0.5#>This book is mine。<#0.8#>第一句中 This 自己站在“谁或什么”的位置，代替一个对象，所以是代词。第二句的 this 后面紧跟 book，它只是帮我们锁定哪本书，不是独立代替 book。<#0.7#>
判断时先别背表格，连续问三件事：这个词指向谁或什么？听者能不能找到它指的对象？它有没有独立站在本来可以放名词短语的位置？三个问题都对上，再判断它在句中负责“谁”“什么”或其他工作。

course.title: Personal pronouns and case
course.meta: Participants and sentence roles
examples: She helped me.
They spoke to him.
The teacher invited Tom and me.
You and I are partners.

exampleNotes.title: Rule focus
exampleNotes.body: She performs the action and takes subject case; me receives it and takes object case.

exampleNotes.title: Rule focus
exampleNotes.body: him is the object of to, so he is not used.

exampleNotes.title: Rule focus
exampleNotes.body: Tom and me forms the object; removing Tom leaves invited me.

exampleNotes.title: Rule focus
exampleNotes.body: You and I forms the subject; removing you leaves I am, not me am.

rules: Personal pronouns identify speaker, listener or others, then change case with grammatical role.
Subject forms normally serve as subjects; object forms serve as verb or preposition objects.
Do not choose case by a politeness formula in coordination; remove the other item and check the remaining role.

questions.question: ___ know the answer.
questions.correct: The blank is the subject, so use They.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: The blank is the subject, so use They.

questions.question: Please wait for ___.
questions.correct: Use us as the object of for.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: Use us as the object of for.

questions.question: The coach praised Ben and ___.
questions.correct: Ben and me is the object of praised.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: Ben and me is the object of praised.

questions.question: ___ will present first.
questions.correct: The whole phrase is subject, so use I.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: The whole phrase is subject, so use I.

narration.text: 两个人搬箱子，一个负责帮忙，一个接受帮助。英语要把这两个位置分清。<#0.4#>She helped me。<#0.8#>She 站在 helped 前，是发出动作的人；me 放在 helped 后，是动作落到的人。两者都指人，但句中任务不同，所以形式不同。作主语的 she 属于主格，作动词宾语的 me 属于宾格。<#0.7#>再听 They spoke to him。They 负责“谁说话”，用主格；him 跟在介词 to 后，作介词宾语，所以用宾格。判断格不能只盯着词离动词近不近，要看它到底占了主语位置，还是被动词、介词支配。<#0.8#>并列时最容易被“礼貌顺序”带偏。The teacher invited Tom and me 中，me 和 Tom 一起接受邀请，所以仍用宾格。You and I are partners 中，I 和 You 一起站在主语位置，所以用主格。<#0.7#>人称代词先区分说话者、听话者和谈到的第三方，再根据位置选格。操作时做两步：先问代词指的是谁；再暂时遮住并列的另一项，只看这个位置负责发出动作，还是接受动词或介词关系。

course.title: Possessive determiners and pronouns
course.meta: Possession in different slots
examples: My book is new.
This book is mine.
Her answer is different from ours.
A friend of mine called.

exampleNotes.title: Rule focus
exampleNotes.body: my marks who owns book and requires the head noun book.

exampleNotes.title: Rule focus
exampleNotes.body: mine stands for my book and does not take book after it.

exampleNotes.title: Rule focus
exampleNotes.body: her requires answer; ours replaces our answer to avoid repetition.

exampleNotes.title: Rule focus
exampleNotes.body: a friend of mine means one of my friends; mine cannot be replaced by my.

rules: my, your, his, her, its, our and their are possessive determiners and require a following noun.
mine, yours, his, hers, ours and theirs are possessive pronouns that replace a possessive determiner plus noun.
Choose by whether the form must stand independently, not merely by the shared Chinese translation “...的”.

questions.question: This is ___ desk.
questions.correct: Use the possessive determiner our before desk.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: Use the possessive determiner our before desk.

questions.question: Their room is large; ___ is small.
questions.correct: ours independently replaces our room.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: ours independently replaces our room.

questions.question: That coat is ___.
questions.correct: No noun follows, so use hers.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: No noun follows, so use hers.

questions.question: He is a classmate of ___.
questions.correct: Use independent mine after of.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: Use independent mine after of.

narration.text: 几本书放在桌上，你拿起一本说 My book is new。my 像一张贴在 book 前的归属标签，必须带着后面的名词一起出现。语法上，my、your、her、our、their 这类叫物主限定词。<#0.8#>如果对方已经知道在谈 book，就可以说 This book is mine。mine 自己占满了“我的书”这个位置，后面不能再接 book。它叫物主代词，功能相当于 my book，但不是把两个词机械拼起来。<#0.7#>再看 Her answer is different from ours。Her 后有 answer，所以用限定形式；ours 跟在 from 后独立出现，指 our answer，所以用代词形式。A friend of mine called 里，mine 也独立放在 of 后，表示“我的朋友之一”，不能换成 my。<#0.8#>两组词中文都常译成“……的”，但英语看的是后面有没有中心名词。his 比较特殊，两种形式写法相同，仍要按位置判断任务；its 通常只作限定形式，英语没有与 mine 平行的独立物主代词。<#0.7#>选择时先看空格后：紧跟名词，就用限定形式；空格本身要代表“谁的某物”，就用独立形式。最后把被省略的名词补回心里读一遍，意思通顺再确定。

course.title: Reflexive pronouns
course.meta: Action returning to the subject or added emphasis
examples: She taught herself.
He looked at himself.
I made the cake myself.
The door opened by itself.

exampleNotes.title: Rule focus
exampleNotes.body: The teacher and learner are the same person, so the action returns to the subject through herself.

exampleNotes.title: Rule focus
exampleNotes.body: The object of at is the same person as he, so use himself rather than him.

exampleNotes.title: Rule focus
exampleNotes.body: the cake is the object; myself only adds “personally” and is not part of a combined object.

exampleNotes.title: Rule focus
exampleNotes.body: by itself means without outside help: the door opened on its own.

rules: Use a reflexive when the subject and the verb or preposition object refer to the same entity.
A reflexive can add emphasis; removing it leaves the sentence core complete.
by oneself means alone or without help, depending on context.

questions.question: Leo cut ___.
questions.correct: Leo both performs and receives the action, so use himself.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: Leo both performs and receives the action, so use himself.

questions.question: She looked at ___ in the mirror.
questions.correct: The reflected object is the subject herself.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: The reflected object is the subject herself.

questions.question: We painted the room ___.
questions.correct: ourselves adds emphasis meaning personally.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: ourselves adds emphasis meaning personally.

questions.question: The robot moved by ___.
questions.correct: by itself means the robot moved without help.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: by itself means the robot moved without help.

narration.text: 镜子前，一个女孩自己教自己弹琴。英语说 She taught herself。动作从 She 发出，又回到同一个人身上，所以不能用 her，而要用 herself。这个带 self 或 selves 的形式叫反身代词。<#0.8#>He looked at himself 也是同样的路线：He 是看的动作发出者，介词 at 后被看的人仍是他本人。即使中间隔着介词，只要动作对象和主语指向同一个人，就用反身形式。<#0.7#>但 I made the cake myself 里的 myself 不承担“做谁”的宾语，它只是强调蛋糕是我亲手做的。删掉 myself，I made the cake 仍然完整。这个用法叫同位强调，位置可以变化，主干不靠它补齐。<#0.8#>The door opened by itself 表示门没有外力帮助，自己开了。by oneself 有时强调独自一人，有时强调没有帮助，要根据场景判断。<#0.7#>操作时先画动作箭头：箭头从主语出发，又回到同一个对象，就用反身代词；若删掉它后主干仍完整，只是少了“亲自”的语气，就是强调用法；看到 by oneself，再问是在说独处，还是在说自行完成。

course.title: Demonstrative pronouns
course.meta: Pointing by distance or discourse
examples: This is my key.
Those are ours.
This idea may work.
He missed the bus. That made him late.

exampleNotes.title: Rule focus
exampleNotes.body: This points to one nearby thing and stands alone as subject.

exampleNotes.title: Rule focus
exampleNotes.body: Those points to several more distant things and agrees with plural are.

exampleNotes.title: Rule focus
exampleNotes.body: This directly determines idea here rather than standing as a pronoun.

exampleNotes.title: Rule focus
exampleNotes.body: That summarizes the whole earlier event of missing the bus.

rules: this/these normally indicate nearer reference and that/those more distant reference, with number agreement.
A demonstrative is a pronoun when independent, and a determiner when directly before a noun.
this and that can refer to an earlier idea or event, not only physical distance.

questions.question: ___ are my shoes over there.
questions.correct: Use Those for several distant shoes.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: Use Those for several distant shoes.

questions.question: In which option is these a pronoun?
questions.correct: These is a pronoun when it stands alone as subject.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: These is a pronoun when it stands alone as subject.

questions.question: I passed the test. ___ made me happy.
questions.correct: That refers to the earlier event of passing.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: That refers to the earlier event of passing.

questions.question: ___ book here is mine.
questions.correct: Use This before the nearby singular noun book.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: Use This before the nearby singular noun book.

narration.text: 找钥匙时，你指着手边的一把说 This is my key；看向远处几双鞋，说 Those are ours。指示词像手指一样把注意力对准对象，同时还告诉听者距离和数量。this 指较近的一个，these 指较近的多个；that 指较远的一个，those 指较远的多个。<#0.8#>第一句中，This 后面没有名词，自己站在主语位置，代替眼前那件东西，所以是指示代词。<#0.7#>接着看 This idea may work。这里 This 紧贴 idea，只负责限定“这个想法”，整个 This idea 才是主语；它在这里是指示限定词。<#0.7#>距离也不一定拿尺子量。He missed the bus。That made him late。这里 That 不是指远处某个物品，而是把前面“错过公交车”整件事打包指回来。对话中 this 和 that 也能组织刚说过或将要说的信息。<#0.8#>判断时先找它指向什么，再核对一个还是多个、语境中较近还是较远；然后看后面是否直接带名词。独立占位置的是代词，带名词的是限定词。最后别忘了检查谓语，不能只顾远近忘了单复数。

course.title: Interrogative pronouns
course.meta: An unknown item filling a sentence slot
examples: Who called you?
Whom did you speak to?
Whose bag is this?
Which do you prefer, tea or coffee?

exampleNotes.title: Rule focus
exampleNotes.body: Who fills the subject slot in who called, so called follows directly.

exampleNotes.title: Rule focus
exampleNotes.body: Whom is the object of to but moves to the front in the question; did marks the question and you remains subject. Everyday English often uses who.

exampleNotes.title: Rule focus
exampleNotes.body: this is the item being identified and serves as subject; Whose bag asks whose bag it is and serves as predicative.

exampleNotes.title: Rule focus
exampleNotes.body: Which is the object of prefer and moves to the front; tea or coffee supplies the limited choice set. what normally asks from an open range.

rules: An interrogative pronoun fills a grammatical role such as subject, object or predicative inside the question.
who asks about people; whom is its object form and is more common formally; whose asks possession.
which selects from a limited set, while what normally asks about an open range of things or content.

questions.question: ___ broke the window?
questions.correct: The blank is the subject of broke, so use Who.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: The blank is the subject of broke, so use Who.

questions.question: To ___ did you send it?
questions.correct: Formal usage takes object-form whom after To.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: Formal usage takes object-form whom after To.

questions.question: ___ coat is yours?
questions.correct: Use Whose to ask possession.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: Use Whose to ask possession.

questions.question: ___ do you want, the red one or the blue one?
questions.correct: The choices are stated, so use Which.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: The choices are stated, so use Which.

narration.text: 电话响了却不知道来电人，你问 Who called you？Who 不是站在句子外贴个“问人”标签，它正占着“谁打来电话”的主语位置，所以后面直接接 called，不需要再添一个主语。这样的疑问词在句内代替未知项，叫疑问代词。<#0.8#>Whom did you speak to？想问的是你和谁说话。you 才是主语，whom 是介词 to 的对象，只因问句结构移到前面。正式语体，尤其介词前置时常用 whom；日常口语中常听到 who。<#0.7#>Whose bag is this 询问所属。这里 this 是要辨认的物品，Whose bag 说明它是谁的包。whose 后带 bag 时有类似限定的作用，但核心仍是把未知的所有者问出来。<#0.8#>桌上只有茶和咖啡两项，问 Which do you prefer, tea or coffee？Which 面向已经限定的范围；如果选项开放，问“你想要什么”，通常用 what。<#0.7#>操作时先把问句还原成带空格的陈述关系：谁做动作，用 who；动作或介词指向谁，正式表达可用 whom；问所属用 whose；给定范围里选用 which，开放询问用 what。再确认疑问词在句内究竟作主语、宾语还是表语。

course.title: Indefinites for unspecified people and things
course.meta: some · any · no · every series
examples: Someone is waiting.
I did not see anything.
Would you like something to drink?
Nobody knows the answer.

exampleNotes.title: Rule focus
exampleNotes.body: Someone denotes one unspecified person and is grammatically singular.

exampleNotes.title: Rule focus
exampleNotes.body: not supplies the negation, while anything keeps the range open to any thing.

exampleNotes.title: Rule focus
exampleNotes.body: Although interrogative in form, this is a positive offer, so something is natural.

exampleNotes.title: Rule focus
exampleNotes.body: Nobody already carries negation, so do not add not; it takes singular knows.

rules: some forms commonly assert an unspecified entity; any forms open the range to any entity and are common in questions, negatives and conditions.
some also appears in requests or offers expecting a positive response, so “questions always take any” is false.
Compound indefinites in no-, every-, -one, -body or -thing normally take singular agreement; no- forms already contain negation.

questions.question: ___ left a message for you.
questions.correct: Someone asserts an unspecified person in an affirmative.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: Someone asserts an unspecified person in an affirmative.

questions.question: I don't need ___.
questions.correct: not supplies negation, so use anything and avoid a double negative.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: not supplies negation, so use anything and avoid a double negative.

questions.question: Would you like ___ to eat?
questions.correct: An offer expecting acceptance commonly uses something.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: An offer expecting acceptance commonly uses something.

questions.question: Everyone ___ ready.
questions.correct: Everyone is grammatically singular.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: Everyone is grammatically singular.

narration.text: 门外传来脚步声，你知道有人，却不知道是谁，可以说 Someone is waiting。Someone 不给出具体身份，只确认“存在某个人”；这类把人或事物留在不确定范围里的词，叫不定代词。它在句中作主语，通常按单数处理，所以用 is。<#0.8#>I did not see anything 里，not 已经表达否定，anything 把范围打开成“任何东西”，合起来就是“什么也没看见”。这里否定已经表达完整，不能再叠加另一个否定词。<#0.7#>问句并非永远只能用 any。端着饮料招待客人时说 Would you like something to drink？说话者在积极提供某样东西，也期待对方接受，所以 something 很自然。普通询问信息、否定或条件中，any 系列更常见。<#0.7#>最后看 Nobody knows the answer。Nobody 自己已经含“没有人”，后面不再加 not，而且它在句中作主语，基础用法配单数 knows。<#0.8#>判断时先看说话者是在确认某个对象存在，还是把范围开放到任何对象；再看否定是否已经由 not 或 no 系列承担；最后检查谓语一致。

course.title: Quantifying indefinite pronouns
course.meta: all · both · each · either · neither · none
examples: Both are correct.
Either will work.
Neither of the answers is correct.
Each has a ticket.
All of the students are ready.
All of the water is clean.
None of the water is left.
None of the students are absent.

analyses.label: Zero members of a plural set

exampleNotes.title: Rule focus
exampleNotes.body: Both includes two entities together and therefore takes plural are.

exampleNotes.title: Rule focus
exampleNotes.body: Either selects either one of two, so basic usage takes singular agreement.

exampleNotes.title: Rule focus
exampleNotes.body: Neither means not one of two; standard basic usage normally takes singular agreement.

exampleNotes.title: Rule focus
exampleNotes.body: Each considers members one by one, so it takes singular has even when many people are involved.

exampleNotes.title: Rule focus
exampleNotes.body: All refers to the whole plural set of students, so it takes are.

exampleNotes.title: Rule focus
exampleNotes.body: All refers to the entire uncountable amount of water, so it takes is.

exampleNotes.title: Rule focus
exampleNotes.body: None means no amount of the uncountable water remains, so it takes is.

exampleNotes.title: Rule focus
exampleNotes.body: None means zero members of the student set are absent; plural are is natural here.

rules: both includes two entities and takes plural agreement as subject.
either means either one of two and normally takes singular agreement in basic usage.
neither means not either one of two and normally takes singular agreement in basic usage.
each considers members individually and normally takes singular agreement.
all denotes a whole range, and agreement follows the plural set or uncountable amount it refers to.
none expresses zero quantity; agreement follows the noun after of and context rather than an “always singular” rule.

questions.question: The two answers are good. ___ are acceptable.
questions.correct: Both includes both answers and takes plural are.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: Both includes both answers and takes plural are.

questions.question: There are two doors. ___ is suitable.
questions.correct: Either means either one of the two and takes singular is.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: Either means either one of the two and takes singular is.

questions.question: ___ of the two answers is correct.
questions.correct: Neither means not either of the two answers.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: Neither means not either of the two answers.

questions.question: ___ of the students has a card.
questions.correct: Each considers students individually and takes has.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: Each considers students individually and takes has.

questions.question: All of the students ___ ready.
questions.correct: All refers to plural students and takes are.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: All refers to plural students and takes are.

questions.question: All of the milk ___ fresh.
questions.correct: All refers to uncountable milk and takes is.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: All refers to uncountable milk and takes is.

questions.question: None of the water ___ left.
questions.correct: water is uncountable, so use is.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: water is uncountable, so use is.

questions.question: None of the players ___ injured.
questions.correct: Here none refers to zero members of plural players, so are is natural.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: Here none refers to zero members of plural players, so are is natural.

narration.text: 桌上有两个答案。说 Both are correct，是把两个一起纳入，所以 Both 配复数 are；说 Either will work，是从两个里任选一个，视角落在“一个”上，基础用法配单数。Neither of the answers is correct 则表示两个中一个也不对，通常也按单数处理。<#0.8#>换成一排学生，Each has a ticket。虽然现场有很多人，Each 像镜头逐个扫过，每次只看一个成员，所以用单数 has。这里决定谓语的不是现实总人数，而是词怎样切分这个范围。<#0.7#>All 要看它后面装的是什么。All of the students are ready 指整个复数学生集合，用 are；All of the water is clean 指全部水量，water 不可数，用 is。<#0.8#>None 表示数量为零，却不是“永远单数”。None of the water is left 跟不可数 water 用 is；None of the students are absent 把复数集合中的缺席人数说成零，用 are 很自然。<#0.7#>判断时先画范围：刚好两个，区分 both、either、neither；逐个看用 each；整个范围用 all；零数量用 none。然后看 of 后的中心名词是复数集合还是不可数数量，再决定谓语。不要只背中文“都、任一、都不”，要看镜头是合看、选一个、逐个看还是看零个。

course.title: Referential and dummy it
course.meta: Sometimes referential, sometimes structural
examples: I bought a phone. It works well.
It is raining.
It is five o’clock.
It is three kilometres to the station.
It is important to rest.
I find it easy to learn online.

exampleNotes.title: Rule focus
exampleNotes.body: It clearly refers back to a phone and answers what works well.

exampleNotes.title: Rule focus
exampleNotes.body: No concrete entity is called it here; it fills the required subject slot in a weather expression.

exampleNotes.title: Rule focus
exampleNotes.body: It refers to no entity; it supplies the subject slot for stating the time.

exampleNotes.title: Rule focus
exampleNotes.body: It does not replace station; it supports the structure stating the distance to the station.

exampleNotes.title: Rule focus
exampleNotes.body: to rest is what is evaluated; it fills the early subject slot and moves the heavier content to the end.

exampleNotes.title: Rule focus
exampleNotes.body: to learn online is the real content of find; it serves as dummy object so easy can follow immediately.

rules: Referential it must have an identifiable antecedent in context.
In weather, time and distance expressions, it normally refers to no entity and fills the subject structure.
Dummy-subject or dummy-object it postpones a longer infinitive or clause, which remains the real content.

questions.question: I found a wallet. ___ was empty.
questions.correct: It refers back to singular wallet.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: It refers back to singular wallet.

questions.question: ___ is snowing.
questions.correct: Weather expressions use dummy It.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: Weather expressions use dummy It.

questions.question: ___ is six o’clock.
questions.correct: Use dummy It to state the time.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: Use dummy It to state the time.

questions.question: ___ is two miles to the beach.
questions.correct: Use dummy It to state distance.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: Use dummy It to state distance.

questions.question: ___ is useful to review daily.
questions.correct: It is dummy subject; to review daily is the real subject.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: It is dummy subject; to review daily is the real subject.

questions.question: We think ___ necessary to leave now.
questions.correct: it is dummy object; to leave now supplies the real content.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: it is dummy object; to leave now supplies the real content.

narration.text: 刚买了一部手机，接着说 I bought a phone。It works well。这里 It 明确指回前面的 a phone，听者能回答“什么运行得好”。这种 it 有具体先行词，承担真正的指代任务。<#0.8#>但窗外下雨时说 It is raining，并没有某个东西叫 it。英语完整句子通常需要主语位置，天气表达就让 it 先把这个位置撑起来。It is five o'clock 表时间，It is three kilometres to the station 表距离，也都不指某件具体物品。<#0.8#>还有一种情况是把太长的内容往后放。It is important to rest 中，真正被评价为 important 的是 to rest；it 先作形式主语，让句子头部轻一些。I find it easy to learn online 里，find 真正涉及的内容是 to learn online，it 先占形式宾语位置，easy 才能自然紧跟。<#0.7#>术语上，要分指代 it、天气时间距离中的无指向 it，以及形式主语或形式宾语 it。<#0.7#>判断时先追问“it 到底指谁或什么”。能在前文找到唯一对象，就是指代用法；找不到，再看是否在说天气、时间、距离；若后面还有不定式或从句，试着把它移到前面，能还原真正内容，就按形式成分分析。

course.title: The two jobs of relative pronouns
course.meta: Linking a clause while representing its antecedent
examples: The girl who sings is Amy.
The book that I bought is useful.
The boy whose bike was lost is sad.
The place where we met is nearby.

analyses.label: Relative clause with who as subject
Relative clause with that as object

exampleNotes.title: Word-order translation
exampleNotes.body: who refers to girl and serves as subject of sings; Chinese moves the modifier before 女孩.

exampleNotes.title: Word-order translation
exampleNotes.body: that refers to book and fills the object gap in I bought ___; Chinese says 我买的书.

exampleNotes.title: Word-order translation
exampleNotes.body: whose shows that bike belongs to boy, and the whole clause postmodifies boy.

exampleNotes.title: Word-order translation
exampleNotes.body: where expresses place inside the clause and is a relative adverb, not a relative pronoun.

rules: A relative pronoun links an antecedent to a relative clause and serves as subject, object or determiner inside the clause.
who normally refers to people, which to things, that to either, and whose to possession; also check the missing role inside the clause.
where, when and why are relative adverbs expressing place, time or reason and should not be classified as relative pronouns.

questions.question: The woman ___ teaches us is kind.
questions.correct: The antecedent is a person and the clause lacks a subject, so use who.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: The antecedent is a person and the clause lacks a subject, so use who.

questions.question: The film ___ we watched was funny.
questions.correct: that refers to film and serves as object of watched.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: that refers to film and serves as object of watched.

questions.question: The student ___ project won smiled.
questions.correct: whose marks the project as belonging to the student.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: whose marks the project as belonging to the student.

questions.question: Which is a relative adverb?
questions.correct: where expresses place and is a relative adverb.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: where expresses place and is a relative adverb.

narration.text: 人群里要说明“那个唱歌的女孩”，英语说 The girl who sings is Amy。who 一头指回 girl，把后面的说明接到女孩身上；另一头又站在 sings 前，承担“谁唱歌”的主语。一个词同时连接外面的名词和填补从句内部位置，这就是关系代词的双重任务。<#0.8#>The book that I bought is useful 里，that 指回 book；从句 I bought 后缺少“买了什么”，that 在内部作宾语。选择关系词不能只看先行词是人还是物，还要检查从句究竟缺主语、宾语还是所属成分。<#0.8#>The boy whose bike was lost is sad 中，whose 把 bike 与 boy 的所属关系带进从句，意思是“他的自行车丢了”。who 常指人，which 常指物，that 可以指人或物，whose 表所属，但具体选择还受句子结构限制。<#0.7#>The place where we met is nearby 的 where 表示“在那里”，在从句中承担地点关系，它是关系副词，不是关系代词；when 和 why 也分别表达时间、原因。<#0.7#>判断时先圈出先行词，再遮住关系词读从句：缺人或物的主语、宾语、所属，就选合适的关系代词；主干成分完整，只缺地点、时间或原因关系，再考虑 where、when、why。

course.title: Reciprocal pronouns
course.meta: Participants acting on one another
examples: The twins help each other.
The players talked to one another.
They looked at themselves.

analyses.label: Reciprocal pronoun as object of preposition
Reflexive pronoun as object of preposition

exampleNotes.title: Rule focus
exampleNotes.body: Each twin helps the other, so the action runs between different participants.

exampleNotes.title: Rule focus
exampleNotes.body: one another is the object of to and shows mutual conversation among the players.

exampleNotes.title: Rule focus
exampleNotes.body: themselves means each person looked at themself, not at the others; this differs from each other.

rules: each other and one another both express mutual action between different participants and are usually interchangeable in modern English.
The key difference from reflexives is whether the action goes to another participant or back to each subject themself.

questions.question: The two friends trust ___.
questions.correct: The friends trust one another, so use each other.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: The friends trust one another, so use each other.

questions.question: The children introduced themselves.

options.text: The action returns to each child

questions.correct: themselves means each child introduced themself.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: themselves means each child introduced themself.

questions.question: The teams competed with ___.
questions.correct: Several teams compete mutually, so use one another.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: Several teams compete mutually, so use one another.

narration.text: 双胞胎一起做作业，一个帮另一个，另一个也帮回来，可以说 The twins help each other。动作不是各自回到自己身上，而是在两个参与者之间来回流动。each other 这种表示彼此作用的形式，叫相互代词。<#0.8#>The players talked to one another 也把说话动作连到其他队员。现代英语中 each other 和 one another 通常可以互换，不必机械规定“两个人只能用前者、三个人以上只能用后者”；真正重要的是场景里至少有不同参与者互相发生作用。<#0.8#>对比 They looked at themselves。这里每个人看的对象是自己，动作分别返回各自主语，所以用反身代词 themselves。前两句是参与者彼此作用，第三句是动作回到各自本人。<#0.7#>判断时画箭头最直接：箭头从一个参与者指向另一个，同时反向发生，用相互代词；箭头从每个主语绕回自己，用反身代词。若动词本身需要介词，还要把介词连同关系一起保留。

course.title: one, ones and the other series
course.meta: Replacing a noun of the same kind, not the same entity
examples: My pen is broken; I need a new one.
These shoes are tight; show me the larger ones.
This cup is dirty; give me another.
One answer is correct; the other is wrong.

analyses.label: ones replacing shoes as direct object

exampleNotes.title: Rule focus
exampleNotes.body: one replaces the noun pen and means a different pen of the same kind.

exampleNotes.title: Rule focus
exampleNotes.body: ones replaces plural shoes, while larger selects the relevant kind.

exampleNotes.title: Rule focus
exampleNotes.body: another means one more or a different singular item of the same class: another cup.

exampleNotes.title: Rule focus
exampleNotes.body: With exactly two, one introduces one item and the other identifies the remaining one.

rules: one/ones replace a countable-noun class and normally mean another item of that kind; it normally refers to the same specific entity.
another means one more or a different singular item in an open set.
For two, use one...the other; for larger sets, one...another...the others can distinguish ranges.

questions.question: My phone is old. I need a new ___.
questions.correct: A new phone of the same kind requires one, not referential it.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: A new phone of the same kind requires one, not referential it.

questions.question: I like the blue shoes, not the red ___.
questions.correct: Use ones to replace plural shoes.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: Use ones to replace plural shoes.

questions.question: This chair is wet. Bring me ___.
questions.correct: Use another for one more singular chair.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: Use another for one more singular chair.

questions.question: There are two keys. One is mine; ___ is yours.
questions.correct: Use the other for the remaining one of two.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: Use the other for the remaining one of two.

narration.text: 手里的笔坏了，你想买一支新的，页面说 My pen is broken；I need a new one。one 代替的是 pen 这一类名词，指同类中的另一支，不是原来那支。<#0.8#>These shoes are tight；show me the larger ones。前面是复数 shoes，所以用 ones，larger 继续说明要同类鞋中更大的那些。one 和 ones 都替代可数名词类别，但要跟着单复数变化。<#0.7#>杯子脏了，要求再拿一个，页面是 This cup is dirty；give me another。another 表示开放范围里的“再一个”或“另一个”单数对象，后面不必重复 cup。<#0.8#>如果范围明确只有两个，就用 One answer is correct；the other is wrong。one 先提出一个，the other 锁定剩下的那个。多于两个时，范围和数量还要随语境继续判断。<#0.7#>操作时先问代词是在指回原来的具体对象，还是替代同类中的另一个；再看单数还是复数、范围是否恰好两个。同类单数或复数看 one、ones，开放范围的另一个看 another，两个中的剩余项看 the other。

course.title: Pronoun–antecedent agreement
course.meta: Matching person, number and known information
examples: Lucy said she was ready.
The students finished their work.
If anyone calls, tell them I am busy.
Every student should bring their ID.

exampleNotes.title: Rule focus
exampleNotes.body: she matches Lucy in person, singular number and known gender information.

exampleNotes.title: Rule focus
exampleNotes.body: their refers back to plural students, so his or her would not match.

exampleNotes.title: Rule focus
exampleNotes.body: The person denoted by anyone has unknown gender, so modern standard English naturally uses singular they/them.

exampleNotes.title: Rule focus
exampleNotes.body: Every student is distributively singular but gender-inclusive; their is a natural inclusive singular reference.

rules: A pronoun should match its antecedent in person and number and respect information established in context.
Use plural pronouns for plural antecedents and do not be distracted by an intervening singular noun.
When gender is unknown, irrelevant or the person uses they, singular they/them/their is standard modern English; keep usage consistent within the context.

questions.question: Mia said ___ would help.
questions.correct: Mia is a known singular female; the blank is clause subject, so use she.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: Mia is a known singular female; the blank is clause subject, so use she.

questions.question: The boys packed ___ bags.
questions.correct: boys is plural, so use their.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: boys is plural, so use their.

questions.question: Someone left ___ umbrella.
questions.correct: The determiner form is required before umbrella; singular their is natural when gender is unknown.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: The determiner form is required before umbrella; singular their is natural when gender is unknown.

questions.question: Every visitor must show ___ ticket.
questions.correct: their inclusively refers back to every visitor.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: their inclusively refers back to every visitor.

narration.text: 接力传话时，代词必须把信息准确交回前面的对象。Lucy said she was ready。she 指回 Lucy，两者都是第三人称单数，语境也已经说明是 Lucy，所以读者不会换错人。这个被代词指回的对象叫先行词，代词要和它在人称、数量及已知信息上协调。<#0.8#>The students finished their work 中，先行词 students 是复数，物主形式就用 their。即使中间出现 work 这样的单数名词，也不能改用 its，因为决定代词的是它真正指向谁，不是离它最近的词。<#0.8#>如果说 If anyone calls, tell them I am busy，anyone 形式上按单数处理，但来电者的性别未知，现代标准英语自然使用单数 they 的宾格 them。Every student should bring their ID 也是逐个学生，却不限定性别，their 是包容而标准的回指。<#0.7#>单数 they 不等于把先行词变成复数；谓语和其他表达仍要按各自结构判断，并在同一语境保持代词形式一致。<#0.7#>检查时先用箭头连出每个代词的先行词，再核对第一、第二、第三人称和单复数；性别未知、不重要或对象使用 they 时，可选 they、them、their。最后从头读一遍，确认没有被中间名词带偏。

course.title: Clear and unambiguous reference
course.meta: The reader should identify the referent immediately
examples: When Tom met Jack, he smiled.
When Tom met Jack, Tom smiled.
Put the vase on the table and clean it.
Students lose focus when they are tired.

analyses.label: Time clause with two male nouns
Time clause clearly referring to students

exampleNotes.title: Rule focus
exampleNotes.body: Both Tom and Jack could be he; the grammar is possible but the referent is unclear.

exampleNotes.title: Rule focus
exampleNotes.body: Repeating Tom is longer but identifies the person precisely; clarity outranks avoiding repetition.

exampleNotes.title: Rule focus
exampleNotes.body: it may refer to vase or table; rewrite with the intended noun.

exampleNotes.title: Rule focus
exampleNotes.body: students is the only suitable plural-human antecedent, so they is clear and repetition is unnecessary.

rules: Even with agreement, a pronoun can be ambiguous when several nearby antecedents match in person and number.
The clearest repair is often to repeat the key noun or rewrite the sentence; do not sacrifice clarity merely to avoid repetition.
Clarity does not ban pronouns; when only one plausible antecedent exists, a pronoun links information naturally.

questions.question: What is the problem with “Lily told Anna that she won”?
questions.correct: Both Lily and Anna could be she.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: Both Lily and Anna could be she.

questions.question: Which is clearer?

options.text: When Ben called Leo, Ben apologized.
When Ben called Leo, he apologized.

questions.correct: Repeating Ben identifies the person who apologized.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: Repeating Ben identifies the person who apologized.

questions.question: Move the box beside the chair and paint it. What should you do?
questions.correct: Both box and chair could be it, so repeat the intended noun.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: Both box and chair could be it, so repeat the intended noun.

questions.question: The players rested because they were tired. Is they clear?
questions.correct: players is the only plausible plural-human antecedent.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: players is the only plausible plural-human antecedent.

narration.text: Tom 遇见 Jack 之后，有人笑了。若只写 When Tom met Jack, he smiled，he 在人称和单数上同时匹配 Tom 与 Jack，语法形式没有错，画面却有两个可能答案。读者不知道是谁笑，这就是指代歧义。<#0.8#>最直接的修复就是页面第二句 When Tom met Jack, Tom smiled。虽然重复了 Tom，却换来了唯一明确的意思。代词的价值是减少重复，但清楚永远比少写一个词更重要。<#0.7#>再看 Put the vase on the table and clean it。it 既可能指 vase，也可能指 table。要消除歧义，就应重复真正要清洁的对象，不能指望读者猜场景。<#0.8#>不过清晰不等于禁止代词。Students lose focus when they are tired 中，前面只有 students 是合理的复数人物先行词，they 指向唯一，使用自然。<#0.7#>检查时从每个代词向前找所有在人称、数量和意义上可能匹配的对象。若候选超过一个，就重复目标名词、调整语序或拆句；若只有一个合理候选，保留代词即可。最后让句子脱离你脑中的画面再读一次，看陌生读者能否立刻确定指向。

course.title: Integrated pronoun decisions
course.meta: Find the referent, then role and range
examples: Every runner checked their number themselves.
I lost my umbrella, so I bought another.
The teacher asked who had finished. Two students raised their hands.
This is the book that I need.
Nina spoke to Emma after Nina arrived.

exampleNotes.title: Rule focus
exampleNotes.body: their refers inclusively to every runner; themselves adds personal emphasis, so the two forms do different jobs.

exampleNotes.title: Rule focus
exampleNotes.body: my requires umbrella; another independently means another umbrella and avoids repetition.

exampleNotes.title: Rule focus
exampleNotes.body: who asks for an unknown person inside the clause; their then clearly refers to two students.

exampleNotes.title: Word-order translation
exampleNotes.body: This points to the present object; that refers to book and is object of need. Chinese moves the modifier before 书.

exampleNotes.title: Rule focus
exampleNotes.body: she could refer to Nina or Emma; repeating Nina identifies the person who arrived immediately.

rules: For any pronoun, ask what it refers to, what role it fills, and whether it denotes the same entity or a substitute of the same kind.
Several pronoun types can appear in one sentence; judge each separately instead of matching Chinese words mechanically.
Finally check that reference agrees and is uniquely identifiable; when unclear, repeat the noun rather than force a pronoun.

questions.question: Every child packed ___ own lunch.
questions.correct: their inclusively refers to every child.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: their inclusively refers to every child.

questions.question: This cup is cracked. Please bring me ___.
questions.correct: A different cup of the same kind requires another.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: A different cup of the same kind requires another.

questions.question: The woman ___ called is my aunt.
questions.correct: who refers to woman and serves as clause subject.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: who refers to woman and serves as clause subject.

questions.question: Nina spoke to Emma after ___ arrived. Which is clearest?
questions.correct: Repeating Nina removes the ambiguity of she.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: Repeating Nina removes the ambiguity of she.

narration.text: 赛前，每位跑者亲自核对号码，可以说 Every runner checked their number themselves。their 指回 every runner，放在 number 前表示所属；themselves 不是宾语，而是强调跑者亲自核对。两个代词靠得很近，任务却完全不同，不能只按中文“他们的、他们自己”机械选词。<#0.8#>I lost my umbrella, so I bought another 里，my 必须带 umbrella；another 独立表示同类中的另一把伞，不是找回原来那把。先问同一个对象还是同类替代，才能在 it 和 another 之间选对。<#0.8#>The teacher asked who had finished。who 在从句内部占主语位置，询问未知的人；下一句 Two students raised their hands，their 又清楚指回复数 students。每出现一个代词，都要重新建立自己的指向和句中任务。<#0.7#>This is the book that I need 中，This 指现场事物，that 一头连 book，一头作 need 的宾语。Nina spoke to Emma after Nina arrived 则故意重复 Nina，因为换成 she 会让两个女性名字都成为候选。<#0.7#>综合判断按三步：先给每个代词画出指向；再看它在句中作主语、宾语、限定、强调还是连接；最后判断它表示原对象、同类替代还是相互关系。完成后再做一次清晰度检查，候选不唯一就重复名词。
